questiontext.text:
Goal

A clerk uses a copy machine to duplicate a form while keeping the original. The registry's machine stamps only the copy. Find the stamp count on both forms afterwards. stamp returns the stamped copy, and stampAndCount returns that copy together with the count still on the original form.

Read
  • Calls. Find the paragraph beginning "In a function call". What does the call allocate after evaluating its arguments? According to the next sentence, what happens to the argument values?
  • Representation of values. Read the first sentence. Which values are self-contained? What does a variable of one of those types store?
Coming from Java

A Java developer might read the new count from the form passed by the caller. The stamping method returns void.

void stamp(Form f) { f.stamps++; }

stamp(mine);
int now = mine.stamps;
Banned: &
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Find new storage in the Calls section. Which form can a call to stamp change?
  • Find self-contained under Representation of values. What does the submitted form contain after the call returns?

testcode.text: c, before := stampAndCount(Form{"Grace Hopper", 3}) fmt.Println(c, before)
f := Form{"Edsger Dijkstra", 0} stamp(f) stamp(f) c, before := stampAndCount(f) fmt.Println(f == Form{"Edsger Dijkstra", 0}, c.Stamps, before)

questiontext.text:
Goal

A signal box controls railway lines and keeps a clock for each timetable. At shift change, two lines exchange timetables, but the clocks stay in place. Swap only the times shown on the clocks. Each clock shows 24-hour time, and tick moves it forward one minute, so 10:59 becomes 11:00 and 23:59 becomes 00:00.

Read
  • Address operators. Read the first paragraph and the paragraph beginning "For an operand x of pointer type". What does &x produce? Which requirement does not apply to a composite literal? What does *x denote?
  • Selectors. Find the first rule after "The following rules apply to selectors". What two types can x have? In each case, what does x.f denote? The depth clause concerns embedding, which appears in topic 19.
  • Assignment statements. Find the sentence beginning "Each left-hand side operand must be". Follow addressable to Address operators. Which operands can appear on the left of an assignment?
Coming from Java

A Java method receives a copy of a reference. Reassigning two parameters therefore changes nothing held by the caller. The method can change only the fields of the referenced objects.

static void swap(Clock a, Clock b) {
    Clock t = a;
    a = b;
    b = t;
}
Required: &
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Before writing newClock, find composite literal under Address operators.
  • Check the signature of swap. What do Address operators say *a and *b denote?

testcode.text: up := newClock(6, 0) down := newClock(18, 30) watch := up swap(up, down) tick(watch) fmt.Println(*up, *down, *watch)
a := newClock(23, 59) b := newClock(23, 59) tick(a) fmt.Println(*a, *b, a == b, *a == *b)

questiontext.text:
Goal

A delivery robot stores its current position and the location of its charging dock. Each robot has its own position, but several robots can share one movable dock. Implement both kinds of update.

Read
  • Pointer types. Read both sentences. What does a pointer reference? What value does a pointer hold before assignment?
  • Selectors. Find the sentence beginning "If x is of pointer type and has the value nil". What happens if the program reads a struct field through that pointer?
  • Representation of values. Find the list beginning "Non-nil pointer, function, slice". What does a pointer value reference? According to the last paragraph, what can happen when two values share data?
Coming from Java

Java accesses every object through a reference, so a field that holds an object shares that object. An immutable record prevents changes to shared state. Go makes the choice explicit in the function signature and field type.

record Position(int row, int col) {}
class Robot { Position at; Dock home; }
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Read the second sentence under Pointer types. What does Home hold when the robot's composite literal omits that field?
  • Find the definition of a pointer value under Representation of values. What does a third robot sharing a dock observe after swapHomes runs?

testcode.text: r := Robot{Name: "R1", At: Position{0, 0}} drive(&r, 1, 2) drive(&r, 2, 0) fmt.Println(r.At, r.Trips)
